blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-migration-1 (`rename_all = "camelCase"` renames every existing field of the public order JSON) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-migration-2 (New required `default_currency` key makes existing `config.toml` files fail to load) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct OrderResponse {
    pub order_id: i64,
    pub customer_id: i64,
    pub total_cents: i64,
findings.recommendation: Remove `#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]` so `GET /orders/{id}` keeps emitting `order_id`, `customer_id` and `total_cents`, and only gains `currency`. Today every partner integration that reads `order_id`, `customer_id` or `total_cents` (as `docs/api.md` still documents them) finds them missing after the deploy, with no BREAKING item in the release note and against the documented rule of two releases of deprecation before a field is renamed. If camelCase is really wanted, it needs its own change: emit both names during the deprecation window, mark it BREAKING, and announce it.
findings.title: `rename_all = "camelCase"` renames every existing field of the public order JSON

findings.evidence:
/// The currency of orders that do not name one (ISO 4217).
pub default_currency: String,
findings.recommendation: Give the field a default (`#[serde(default = "default_currency")]` returning `"EUR"`, the currency every existing order was in), and test that a config without the key still loads. Today `config::load` returns `missing field `default_currency`` for every deployed `config.toml` written before this change, so the service refuses to start on upgrade; the release note says nothing about a manual step. If the key must stay required, mark it BREAKING in the release note with the line operators must add.
findings.title: New required `default_currency` key makes existing `config.toml` files fail to load
